name: FasterCable, Inc.
old_description: Special Dealer Pricing Available for Volume Purchases (Click Here)
about:
FasterCable, Inc. operates from Las Vegas, Nevada, supplying electrical and automation components through its web-based catalog. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or ownership structure.

Its product lineup centers on cable and wire management: Lutze Silflex A308 tray-rated control cable and DRIVEFLEX shielded VFD cable, Fastercable-branded 24 AWG 1.5-pair and 22 AWG 2-conductor plenum shielded low-capacitance cables, Hellermann Tyton cable ties in 12- and 15-inch lengths and narrow-slot wire duct in 2x5, 3x5, and 4x5 sizes. The catalog also includes Chevron Phillips Chemical plenum pneumatic tubing, Finder DPDT relays with 24 VAC or 12 VDC coils and matching DIN-rail sockets, and Altech Corp 24 VDC DIN-rail power supplies rated at 96 W.

The company targets electrical contractors, panel shops, and OEMs that purchase in volume, advertising special dealer pricing for larger orders. A downloadable catalog and a request-a-catalog option support product selection.

FasterCable positions itself as a multi-brand distributor that consolidates cables, wire duct, relays, tubing, and power supplies into a single online storefront.

name: Faytex Corporation
old_description: Since 1978, Faytex Corp. has delivered quality footwear, apparel and equipment fabrics as well as outstanding customer
about:
Faytex Corporation, headquartered in Weymouth, Massachusetts, was founded in 1978 by Bill Fay Sr. Since its inception, the company has focused on delivering quality footwear, apparel, and equipment fabrics backed by customer service and sensible pricing.

Faytex develops and manufactures performance fabrics engineered for footwear environments, including moisture-management technologies such as Dri-Lex (introduced in 1988) and the patented Dri-Lex Aerospacer (1989). The company also offers an Eco range of verifiable, eco-friendly fabrics for the shoe industry. Its capabilities span fabric development, sampling through fabric books, and collaborative product design from inception to delivery. In 2012, the company accelerated its innovation cadence, launching close to a dozen new fabrics.

The company serves the footwear, apparel, and equipment industries, working with brands and manufacturers that require specialized fabrics for shoes, clothing, and gear. Its customer base includes footwear brands seeking innovative materials for performance and sustainability.

Faytex states that its differentiation lies in deep footwear expertise, patented fabric technologies, and a partnership approach that adds value by identifying end-consumer needs throughout the product lifecycle.

about:
Feldkamp's Furniture operates from its Salina, Kansas location as part of a six-store chain serving central Kansas. The company's history and founding year are not disclosed in its public materials, nor are details about ownership structure or founders.

The business functions as a full-line home furnishings retailer, carrying mattresses, sofas, dining sets, bedroom suites, home office furniture, decor accents, reclining and leather furniture, sectionals, fireplaces, kids' bedroom sets, and outdoor pieces. Its showroom and website feature major brands such as Beautyrest and Signature Design by Ashley, and the company promotes in-store same-day take-home savings, financing options, and a dedicated clearance section.

The retailer targets residential consumers seeking mid‑range to premium furniture and bedding. Product listings highlight specific models like the Beautyrest 2025 Level 2 Medium Firm Pillow Top and the Ashley Midnight‑Madness corduroy living room set, indicating a focus on brand‑name merchandise for everyday home use.

Feldkamp's emphasizes convenience through its six physical locations, same‑day pickup promotion, flexible financing, and a clearance area for discounted inventory. These service‑oriented differentiators are presented as the primary reasons customers choose the store.

The company specializes in handcrafted metal art and custom fabrication, employing a team of craftsmen to produce one-of-a-kind metalwork. While specific facility size and production volumes are not disclosed, the operation centers on bespoke projects rather than high-volume runs.

The firm emphasizes its craft-driven approach, with Andrew Ferrin highlighting a passion for beautiful custom metal pieces as the foundation of the business. This artisan-focused philosophy distinguishes the shop in a market often dominated by automated production.

name: Fetzer Woodworking
old_description: Kasper Fetzer started a small cabinet shop in downtown Salt Lake City over 100 years ago. Today, Fetzer Architectural Woodwork leads the industry with exceptional woodwork designs and quality
about:
Fetzer Architectural Woodwork operates from West Valley City, Utah, tracing its roots to 1909 when Kasper Fetzer opened a modest cabinet shop in downtown Salt Lake City. The company remains privately held, though the current ownership structure is not publicly detailed.

The firm specializes in architectural millwork and custom woodwork design, producing everything from veneered wall panels to complex translucent composite resin assemblies. It describes itself as one of the largest millworkers in the nation, though specific facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not disclosed.

Its project portfolio spans retail flagships (Brooks Brothers, Banana Republic, DKNY, Ugg), luxury hospitality (Four Seasons, Marriott, Hyatt Regency, Mandarin Oriental), corporate headquarters (Haynes Boone, Huntsman Capital, Devon Energy), institutional landmarks (LDS Conference Center, Public Library, Federal Courthouse, City Hall), performing arts venues (Alice Tully Hall, Symphony Hall), and marine interiors (Seahawk Yacht).

Fetzer emphasizes collaborative innovation with architects, designers, and contractors. A noted breakthrough came on the Alice Tully Hall project, where craftsmen applied wood veneer to a translucent composite resin to create backlit wood panels—a technique the company says had never been done before.

name: Field to Fabric Quilt Company
old_description: Field to Fabric is an award winning specialty quilt shop located in
about:
Field to Fabric Quilt Company operates as an award-winning specialty quilt shop in downtown Winfield, Kansas. The business provides a full range of quilting supplies and offers longarm machine quilting services to customers throughout the region.

The shop distinguishes itself as the only quilt retailer in Kansas dedicated to DIY t-shirt quilts, assisting makers with project completion using a wide selection of color blenders. Inventory includes fabric by the bolt, notions, books, embroidery floss, and cross-stitch materials, alongside a rotating assortment of pre-cut quilt kits. A classroom space hosts regular sewing events, including monthly hand-work sessions and community shop-hop activities.

Field to Fabric serves individual quilters, crafters, and sewing enthusiasts rather than industrial buyers. The shop participates in the Central Kansas Quilt Shop Hop, the Border Run shop hop with stores in Wellington, Burden, and Ponca City, and the All Kansas/Nebraska Quilt Shop Hop, drawing visitors from across the multi-state region. These events feature exclusive fabrics, block kits, and finishing kits designed by the shop.

The company emphasizes project completion support, offering longarm quilting, color-blending guidance, and a schedule of open sewing days to help customers finish works in progress. Its focus on t-shirt quilt conversion and participation in regional hop events reflect a community-oriented approach to the craft retail market.

name: Fiesta Plastics Inc
about:
Fiesta Plastics Inc. opened in 1988 in Mesa, Arizona, when founder Jack Thompson traded the title of his truck for a small injection molding machine after three decades in the plastics industry. Within months the machine was paid off and three more followed, laying the groundwork for a company that has grown steadily for over 30 years.

Today the 20,000-square-foot facility houses 19 injection molding machines ranging from 25 to 650 tons with shot sizes up to 7.5 pounds. The shop processes a wide range of thermoplastics including ABS, acetal, acrylic, HIPS, nylon, polycarbonate, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyurethane, PVC, and TPU. In-house tooling capabilities center on two Fadal high-speed machining centers, supporting mold production from simple mud sets to Class A tools, along with mold maintenance and repair. Product and mold design are handled in SolidWorks 2024, accepting Part, STEP, IGES, and STL files, while rapid prototyping is available via 3D printing in both plastic and metal materials.

The company serves customers needing a complete finished product, from micro-molded components to large complex assemblies. Its blog notes core competencies in mold building, injection molding, assembly, and value-added operations across a variety of part sizes and complexities.

Fiesta Plastics emphasizes a “Never Give Up” motto built on quality at an economical price, continual innovation, customer satisfaction as the top priority, and integrity in every interaction. The firm positions itself as a full-service partner rather than a molding shop alone, handling design, manufacturing, and delivery under one roof.

name: Fine Wood Works
old_description: Fine Woodworks offers a one stop shop. Design & build what you dream – built in cabinetry, furniture, architectural millwork, front entrance systems and etc…
about:
Fine Wood Works is a family-owned cabinet shop based in Piedmont, Missouri. Founded in 2006 by Lucas and Sara Edgy, the business traces its roots to Lucas’s college years when he built bookcases and small cabinets for friends. By 2003 he was working full-time as a cabinetmaker in Piedmont, and two years later the couple opened Fine Wood Works. In 2006 they purchased 30 acres with a barn, which they remodeled into the current woodworking facility.

The company designs, builds, and installs custom cabinetry, furniture, architectural millwork, and front entrance systems for residential and commercial projects. Operating from an 11,000-square-foot shop expanded over the years — including a dedicated spray finishing room, sanding area, and countertop fabrication space — the team uses KCD software to create 3D cabinet presentations, a practice Lucas adopted early in the region. All work is completed in-house from design through installation.

Fine Wood Works serves homeowners undertaking kitchen, bathroom, and living-room remodels, as well as builders on new-home and commercial projects. Client testimonials reference projects in Town & Country, Missouri, and highlight collaboration with Lucas on custom islands, laundry rooms, and dining tables.

The shop emphasizes its guarantee to stand by craftsmanship and protect its reputation, promising to go the extra mile if quality falls short. Lucas notes that the business relies on customer referrals, and many clients return for additional projects.
